Training and Live Monitoring Thresholds for Sebuleni Pro Max AI

This file converts the earlier prevention guidance into concrete operating thresholds and decision rules. These are recommended starting defaults for the first stable version of the platform, not permanent constants. It now reflects the clarified operating context: one selected instrument at a time, raw 1-minute OHLC input, higher timeframes built by resampling, and event logic based on price difference rather than generic variable movement.

Contents

  1. Operating assumptions
  2. Training data and label gates
  3. Training monitoring thresholds
  4. Model promotion rules
  5. Live deployment monitoring
  6. Rollback and retraining triggers
  7. What to enforce first

Operating assumptions

The thresholds below assume the system follows the project design already established: chronological train, validation, and test separation; self-supervised pre-event labeling from price moves; multi-timeframe learning from 1m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d; higher timeframes built by OHLC resampling; a shared backbone with specialized heads; regime-sensitive adaptation; and training-only historical analogy retrieval during evaluation.

They also assume the model learns from the full training range, not from a reduced subset. Validation remains for stopping, selection, and calibration decisions. Test remains untouched until final evaluation or controlled post-deployment backtesting.

How to use these numbers

Treat each threshold as one of three kinds: a hard gate that blocks promotion, a warning band that forces review, or a trigger that automatically changes system behavior such as rollback, reduced confidence, or retraining.

Training data and label gates

Data quality thresholds

Check Threshold Severity Required action
Duplicate timestamps in base 1-minute OHLC or any derived timeframe 0 allowed Blocker Stop training and repair source data before generating windows.
Rows out of chronological order 0 allowed after preprocessing Blocker Resort and revalidate full timeframe before any feature computation.
Missing bars ratio per timeframe <= 0.5% acceptable, 0.5% to 2% warning, > 2% block Gate Above warning, add missingness features and inspect gap causes. Above block, do not train until repaired or segmented.
Longest consecutive gap <= 3 bars acceptable, 4 to 12 warning, > 12 block for that timeframe segment Gate Split segments or mask affected windows. Never forward-fill long structural gaps as if nothing happened.
Extreme candle anomalies by robust z-score |z| > 8 flag, |z| > 12 likely defect Warning Review whether the spike is genuine event data or bad data. Clip only confirmed defects, not real extremes.
Feature scaling fit scope Training-only statistics Blocker If validation or test contributes to scaler statistics, discard run and rebuild pipeline.

Self-supervised label thresholds

Label rule Starting threshold Why it exists Action if broken
Positive event persistence Price move must remain beyond threshold for at least 2 consecutive bars in the target timeframe Prevents one-bar price spikes from becoming meaningful event labels Increase persistence or raise event threshold
Event cool-down Minimum separation of 25% of the forecast horizon between labeled events Prevents one volatile episode from being labeled as many separate positives Merge nearby events into one episode
Positive pre-event window end Positive window must end at least 1 bar before price-move onset Forces the model to learn precursor OHLC state, not event onset contamination Drop any positive sample that overlaps with onset
Ambiguous zone exclusion Exclude windows within 10% of horizon distance from incomplete or overlapping events Reduces mislabeled negatives and positives Mask ambiguous windows rather than forcing a class
Positive class share 2% to 25% preferred, < 1% severe imbalance, > 35% likely threshold too loose Protects against both rarity collapse and over-labeling noise Adjust threshold, horizon, or class weighting strategy

Training monitoring thresholds

Optimization and generalization controls

Metric or rule Starting threshold Severity Required response
Gradient norm after clipping Clip at 1.0 Standard Keep clipping active from the first run to stabilize Transformer and multi-head training.
Backbone learning rate Start at 1e-4 Standard Lower to 5e-5 if validation becomes unstable.
Head learning rate Start at 3e-4 Standard Reduce if heads overfit faster than backbone.
Weight decay 1e-4 for backbone, 5e-5 for heads Standard Increase moderately if train/validation gap widens early.
Dropout 0.10 to 0.20 in backbone, 0.15 to 0.25 in heads Standard If validation improves but calibration worsens, prefer more dropout before more model size.
Early stopping patience for backbone pretraining 8 validation checks Gate Stop if no meaningful validation improvement beyond 0.3%.
Early stopping patience for heads 6 validation checks Gate Heads tend to overfit faster, so stop earlier.
Train vs validation AUC gap on event head <= 0.05 healthy, 0.05 to 0.08 warning, > 0.08 overfit Gate Reduce model capacity, strengthen regularization, or revise labels.
Train vs validation F1 gap on event head <= 0.07 healthy, > 0.10 block promotion Gate Do not promote a model with inflated training performance.
Boundary coverage PICP at 90% interval 0.88 to 0.93 target band, < 0.85 poor, > 0.95 too wide Gate If too low, uncertainty is underestimated. If too high, intervals are too loose to be useful.
Expected Calibration Error <= 0.03 strong, 0.03 to 0.06 warning, > 0.06 block Gate Recalibrate on validation outputs and do not promote until fixed.

MoE, regime, and cross-timeframe monitoring

Monitor Threshold Meaning Response
Expert routing concentration Any one expert serving > 70% of samples for 3 consecutive epochs is warning; > 85% is failure Possible expert collapse or ineffective gating Add load-balancing loss, reduce expert count, or delay expert specialization.
Unused experts Any expert receiving < 5% of routing mass for 5 epochs Wasted capacity or unstable specialization Prune or retrain routing with stronger balancing.
Cross-timeframe OHLC consistency score >= 0.80 target, 0.70 to 0.80 warning, < 0.70 block Measures whether lower and higher frames are aligned enough to trust the hierarchy Review alignment pipeline and cross-attention configuration.
Regime false alarm rate on validation <= 5% target, 5% to 8% warning, > 8% block Too many spurious regime changes Increase persistence threshold and reduce detector sensitivity.
Regime detection delay <= 5 time steps target, > 8 warning Detector is too slow to be useful operationally Rebalance sensitivity versus false alarms.

Model promotion rules

A model should only move from training to staging, or from staging to production, if it clears all hard gates simultaneously. Passing a single attractive metric is not enough in this system because event detection, timing, calibration, regime detection, and explanation quality all affect downstream trust.

Promotion gate 1

No leakage violations, no blocked data-quality issues, and no training-only artifacts fitted on validation or test.

Promotion gate 2

Event head validation F1 must meet the target for the chosen timeframe setup, with no major train-validation gap.

Promotion gate 3

Calibration, interval coverage, and regime false alarm rate must all fall inside acceptable bands.

Promotion gate 4

Explanation retrieval during validation must use training-only memory and show stable analogy precision.

Minimum release standard

Do not promote if any of the following are true: event AUC gap above 0.08, F1 gap above 0.10, ECE above 0.06, PICP below 0.85, regime false alarm rate above 8%, or expert routing concentration above 85%.

Live deployment monitoring

Latency and system health

Live metric Threshold Severity Action
Total inference latency <= 80ms healthy, 80 to 100ms warning, > 100ms critical Operational Above critical, degrade to lighter retrieval or suppress non-essential explanation detail.
Dynamics backbone latency <= 30ms target Operational If exceeded for 5 consecutive minutes, investigate model size or hardware contention.
Similarity retrieval latency <= 20ms target, > 30ms warning Operational Reduce analog count temporarily from 200 to 50 if needed.
Missing incoming 1-minute bars or failed resample updates > 3 consecutive missing bars in any active timeframe is warning; > 12 is critical Data Flag degraded mode, widen intervals, and lower confidence outputs.

Prediction quality and drift

Live monitor Threshold Interpretation Action
Rolling event error increase versus 30-day baseline > 15% warning, > 25% critical Model is losing local fit Enter review mode at warning; start shadow retraining at critical.
Rolling MAE or RMSE increase per timeframe > 20% warning, > 30% critical relative to baseline Dynamics drift or degraded input quality Check timeframe-specific data quality and drift scores.
Novelty score > 2.5 warning, > 3.5 critical on normalized scale Current latent state is far from known historical behavior Widen intervals, reduce confidence, and log for regime review.
Drift score persistence Critical only if above threshold for 5 consecutive inference cycles Separates real shift from one-off disturbance Only persistent drift may trigger regime adaptation.
Event probability jump without cross-timeframe OHLC confirmation Increase of > 0.35 in 3 cycles while higher frames disagree Likely noisy short-term pulse Mark as unstable signal and suppress high-confidence alerting.
Confidence floor If final confidence 0.55, do not issue strong event alert Prediction may be informational but not actionable Return soft warning only.
Analogy support count < 30 strong analogs is weak support; < 10 is critical weak support Explanation is too thin to justify high-confidence claims Reduce confidence and label explanation as low-evidence.

Alert severity rules

The live system should use three alert levels. Advisory means one metric is outside the healthy band but the forecast remains usable. Warning means there is meaningful degradation and the forecast should carry reduced confidence or degraded mode labels. Critical means either system safety, data validity, or model reliability is compromised enough that automated adaptation, rollback, or prediction suppression must be considered immediately.

Rollback and retraining triggers

Trigger Threshold Action Notes
Post-update performance drop in shadow evaluation Event F1 down by > 5% or ECE up by > 0.02 Reject update before promotion Never promote an online update that wins on one metric but loses on calibration.
Production model degradation after update Rolling error up > 10% for 3 consecutive monitoring windows Automatic rollback to last good checkpoint Keep at least 5 signed good checkpoints.
Regime false alarm explosion False alarm rate doubles versus 30-day baseline Rollback detector or increase persistence threshold immediately This often signals over-sensitive adaptation rather than genuine change.
Confidence miscalibration in live backfill ECE above 0.08 for 2 consecutive daily evaluations Freeze deployment branch and recalibrate Do not allow confidence outputs to drift silently.
Weak analogy support during high-confidence price-move forecasts Confidence > 0.80 but analog support count < 20 Force confidence cap at 0.65 until reviewed High certainty without evidence is not acceptable in this system.
Sustained novelty Novelty score above 3.5 for 5 consecutive cycles and error up > 25% Start shadow retraining and new-regime candidate evaluation Do not create a new regime from novelty alone. Require performance deterioration too.
Threshold policy change by user Any material change in event magnitude threshold or horizon Recompute labels and revalidate event head before deployment Fine-tuning only the event head is acceptable if backbone assumptions remain valid.
Safe adaptation rule

Adapt only when three conditions hold together: performance deterioration exceeds threshold, the drift or novelty signal persists long enough to rule out a transient shock, and the proposed update beats the incumbent model on a protected shadow validation slice.

What to enforce first

  1. Hard-stop all leakage paths, including scaler fitting, calibration fitting, and explanation index contamination.
  2. Enforce data quality gates before training starts, especially timestamp order, duplicate removal, and gap controls.
  3. Protect the self-supervised label builder with persistence, cool-down, and ambiguity exclusion rules.
  4. Use train-versus-validation gap thresholds as promotion blockers, not as advisory-only signals.
  5. Monitor calibration and analogy support in production with the same seriousness as accuracy.
  6. Require persistence before any regime change or MoE specialization is allowed to alter the production path.

If only a few thresholds are implemented first, I would start with these six: duplicate timestamps must be zero, missing bar ratio above 2% blocks training, event AUC gap above 0.08 blocks promotion, ECE above 0.06 blocks promotion, novelty above 3.5 plus error increase above 25% triggers shadow retraining, and live latency above 100ms triggers degraded mode. In this project, all six should be interpreted through the lens of single-instrument OHLC behavior rather than a generic multivariate dataset.
